testCacheIDPForLogin assumes at least one organization already exists in the realm and calls getAll().get(0), which throws IndexOutOfBoundsException when the test runs in isolation with no organizations — an ordering dependency on test execution state

remove() performs unconditional delegate lookup (getByAlias) before the isInvalid check, adding a redundant DB hit on cache-served removals instead of reusing the in-scope cached model

Cache-hit path in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin returns unwrapped IdentityProviderModels, bypassing the organization-aware wrapper applied on cache misses, causing inconsistent authorization-relevant behavior between cached and uncached responses

New predicate arm in getLoginPredicate drops member-only (non-BROKER_PUBLIC) organization brokers from all fetch modes, including ALL mode scoped to the matching organizationId, removing existing login capability for org members

InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider getForLogin idp == null fallback branch (cache invalidation and re-read) is never triggered by any test

OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean's idp.isEnabled() re-filter has no test creating a disabled-but-org-linked IDP to assert it is absent from the login page bean output

Predicate change in IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getLoginPredicate() silently reclassifies every existing org-linked IDP lacking BROKER_PUBLIC config, dropping them from getForLogin results on deploy with no backfill or feature flag

Test cleanup registers the wrong alias literal 'alias' instead of 'idp-alias-' + i, so no IDPs created by testCacheIDPForLogin are cleaned up and persist into subsequent tests

Cached results in getForLogin skip the organization-aware wrapping, so the same call returns different IDP models depending on cache state — cache-miss path returns wrapped models while cached path returns plain IdentityProviderModel instances, causing organization-aware behavior (e.g., hiding/marking org-linked IDPs) to disappear once the cache warms

NPE in getLoginPredicate when getConfig() is null and the IDP is org-linked — the predicate dereferences idp.getConfig().get(...) without a null check on the config, causing registerIDPLoginInvalidation to throw NPE during create/update/remove operations for programmatic/legacy models with null config

Cache entry rebuilt with cache.getCurrentCounter() while the initial build uses startupRevision in the multi-search branch — inconsistent revision bases may cause addRevisioned to reject or clobber entries, silently degrading org-scoped login lookups to uncached behavior on clustered deployments

Cache-key thrash in getForLogin: every new organizationId invalidates and rewrites the whole login query entry for that FetchMode, causing repeated invalidate/DB-read/rewrite cycles in realms with many organizations, and the query object's IDP-set map grows unboundedly with org count until the next global invalidation

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test cleanup registers get("alias") — a fabricated identifier for all 20 created IDPs — so cleanup removes a nonexistent resource and leaves 20 persistent IDPs in the shared test realm, breaking subsequent tests and causing duplicate-alias errors on re-run; should use get("idp-alias-" + i)

Inconsistent revision argument to addRevisioned in getForLogin's extend-existing branch: uses cache.getCurrentCounter() instead of startupRevision, diverging from the established query-caching pattern and defeating the cache on mixed search sequences

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show an inconsistency in `getForLogin`: when `query == null` it calls `cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision)`, but when extending an existing cached entry for a new `searchKey` (`cached == null` branch) it calls `cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter())`. Whether this actually “defeats the cache” can’t be verified from the diff alone (it depends on `addRevisioned`/revision semantics not shown), but the mismatch is real and merits review for correctness/consistency with other caching patterns.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove() now performs an unconditional delegate lookup (idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)) even when the alias cache entry is valid, adding a permanent storage hit to every IDP removal that previously could be served from cache

adjudication.rationale: Verified in the diff: remove(String alias) now unconditionally executes `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` before checking `isInvalid(cacheKey)`. Previously, the delegate lookup was only done inside the `if (isInvalid(cacheKey))` branch. This introduces a guaranteed delegate/storage hit on every removal even when the alias cache entry is valid, which is a concrete performance/regression concern but not a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testCacheIDPForLogin assumes at least one organization already exists in the realm and calls getAll().get(0), which throws IndexOutOfBoundsException when the test runs in isolation with no organizations — an ordering dependency on test execution state

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added test `testCacheIDPForLogin`, the line `String orgaId = testRealm().organizations().getAll().get(0).getId();` unconditionally indexes the first organization. The diff does not show the test creating an organization beforehand, so the test implicitly relies on external setup/state (e.g., realm preloaded with at least one org). That makes the test potentially fragile if `getAll()` can be empty, but whether it actually is empty in this test environment isn’t verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cached path in getForLogin final loop returns unwrapped IdentityProviderModels, diverging from the delegate path's wrapping via createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, causing login behavior to differ between warm and cold cache

adjudication.rationale: In `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin`, the cache-miss path explicitly wraps results via `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`, but the cache-hit path reconstructs results by iterating cached IDs and doing `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and returns `identityProviders.stream()` without an explicit `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` mapping. The diff alone doesn’t prove that `getById` returns an unwrapped model (it could already wrap internally), but it does show an asymmetry between warm vs cold paths that could lead to different model types/behavior depending on cache state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OrganizationCacheTest cleanup registers wrong alias 'alias' instead of 'idp-alias-' + i, leaking 20 IDPs into the shared test realm and polluting subsequent tests

adjudication.rationale: In `OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin`, after creating each IDP in the `for (int i = 0; i < 20; i++)` loop, the cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` even though the created aliases are `"idp-alias-" + i`. The same incorrect cleanup registration appears again after creating `idp-alias-20`. This means the cleanup will try to remove an IDP with alias literal `"alias"` (likely non-existent) and will not remove the created IDPs, leaking them into the shared test realm and potentially affecting subsequent tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test covers the mixed-search reuse branch (query != null && cached == null) in getForLogin, the most concurrency-sensitive code in the diff

adjudication.rationale: In `getForLogin`, the branch `query != null` followed by `cached = query.getIDPs(searchKey); if (cached == null) { ... }` only triggers when the same `cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)` already exists but a *new* `searchKey` (derived from `organizationId`) is requested for that same `mode`. The added test `testCacheIDPForLogin` populates caches for `REALM_ONLY` with `organizationId=null` (searchKey=""), and for `ORG_ONLY`/`ALL` only with a single `orgaId`—it never calls `getForLogin` twice with the same `FetchMode` but different `organizationId` values. Therefore, the mixed-search reuse path (`query != null && cached == null`) is not covered by tests, despite being nontrivial cache invalidation logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove() performs unconditional delegate lookup (getByAlias) before the isInvalid check, adding a redundant DB hit on cache-served removals instead of reusing the in-scope cached model

adjudication.rationale: In remove(String alias), the diff adds `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` before `if (isInvalid(cacheKey)) { ... } else { ... }`. This means the delegate lookup happens even when the alias cache key is valid and a `CachedIdentityProvider` could have been used to drive invalidation, making the delegate call potentially redundant for cache-served removals. This is a performance/efficiency concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getLoginPredicate change drops org-linked non-BROKER_PUBLIC IDPs for all storage providers, not just the new cache, with no test verifying non-cached (JPA/map) getForLogin results under the new exclusion

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the global SPI-level `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` to additionally require `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))` (server-spi change). That predicate is not cache-specific and will affect `getForLogin` behavior for all storage providers that rely on `getLoginPredicate`, not just the new Infinispan caching added in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider`. The added test (`OrganizationCacheTest#testCacheIDPForLogin`) focuses on cache population/invalidation and only creates org-linked IDPs with `BROKER_PUBLIC=true`; it does not assert the non-cached (delegate) `getForLogin` results or the behavior for org-linked `BROKER_PUBLIC=false` IDPs under the new predicate.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove() does not invalidate login caches when the IDP lookup returns null but a stale cache entry exists, leaving login pages listing removed IDPs

adjudication.rationale: In `remove(String alias)`, login-cache invalidation is driven solely by `storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` and `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)`. If that delegate lookup returns `null` (e.g., backing store already missing the IDP) while some cache state may still reference the IDP (alias/by-id/login list entries), `registerIDPLoginInvalidation` becomes a no-op because `getLoginPredicate()` includes `Objects::nonNull`. Unlike the IDP invalidation path, which may use the cached entry when `isInvalid(cacheKey)` is false, the login-cache invalidation never falls back to the cached IDP, so login caches can remain stale in this scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getLoginPredicate() semantics changed (filtering out org-linked non-public IDPs) in a PR intended to add caching, affecting all storage providers including the non-cached JPA path, without justification, changelog, or tests for non-cached paths

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes global semantics of `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` by adding `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))` in `server-spi`, which affects all storage provider implementations (not just the new Infinispan caching path). The added tests (`OrganizationCacheTest#testCacheIDPForLogin`) exercise caching behavior and cache invalidation, but do not directly validate this predicate change across non-cached/JPA paths. This is a concrete scope/architecture concern created by the diff, though it is not provably a correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Login cache is not invalidated when an IDP's organization membership changes via OrganizationIdentityProviderProvider paths (addIdentityProvider/removeIdentityProvider/removeById), leaving stale internalId sets in .idp.login caches

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds .idp.login caching plus invalidation hooks on IDP create/update/remove (registerIDPLoginInvalidation / registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate) inside InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider. However, the finding specifically alleges missing invalidation when organization membership changes via OrganizationIdentityProviderProvider paths (addIdentityProvider/removeIdentityProvider/removeById). Those code paths are not shown in this diff, so it’s not verifiable here whether they do or do not trigger IDP updates/invalidation. The added test even asserts caches are cleared after an org-link operation, implying some invalidation may exist elsewhere, but that implementation is خارج the shown diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove() now performs an unconditional uncached delegate read (getByAlias) on every remove even when the alias cache is valid, when the cached instance would suffice for registerIDPLoginInvalidation

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `remove(String alias)` now always executes `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` before checking `isInvalid(cacheKey)`, meaning an unconditional delegate read occurs even when the alias cache is valid. Previously, `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` was only called in the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` branch. This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/architecture regression (extra DB/store hit) rather than a correctness defect; the cached `CachedIdentityProvider` in the valid-cache branch might have been usable to decide whether to call `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(...)` (though the diff doesn’t prove it contains all needed fields).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test cleanup registers get("alias") which doesn't match created aliases (idp-alias-0..20), leaking 21 IDPs into subsequent tests and causing order-dependent failures

adjudication.rationale: In OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin, the loop creates IDPs with aliases "idp-alias-" + i, but registers cleanup as testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove (literal "alias"), which does not match any created alias. The same incorrect cleanup is added again for idp-alias-20. This means the created IDPs will not be removed by cleanup, leaking them into subsequent tests and causing order-dependent failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test coverage for the getForLogin fallback path where a cached internalId's getById returns null (stale cached entry referencing a removed IDP), the sole correctness mechanism for the invalidation window

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a fallback path in `getForLogin` where, when iterating cached internalIds, `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` can return null; in that case it registers invalidation and falls back to `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...)` (see new block around `if (idp == null) { realmCache.registerInvalidation(cacheKey); return idpDelegate.getForLogin(...) ... }`). The added test `testCacheIDPForLogin` exercises cache population and invalidation behaviors, but it never creates a scenario where the login cache contains an internalId that later becomes missing (stale) without the cache being invalidated first; removals of login-eligible IDPs would trigger `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(...)` and clear the cache, and the only explicit removal in the test is for a non-login-eligible IDP (`idp-alias-1`), which would not be present in the cached set. Therefore, the specific null-`getById` fallback branch is not covered by tests in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Login-cache invalidation depends on all org-membership mutations routing through IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update(), but org linking via OrganizationProvider (addIdentityProvider/unlink/org removal cascade) may bypass it, leaving stale IDP membership in login caches

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new revisioned cache for `getForLogin()` keyed only by realm+FetchMode (`cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)`) with per-organization results stored inside `IdentityProviderListQuery` under `searchKey` (organizationId). Invalidation for these login caches is only registered on IDP `create()`/`remove()` (`registerIDPLoginInvalidation`) and on IDP `update()` (`registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate`, based on login predicate and `original.getOrganizationId()` change). The diff shows no explicit invalidation hook for organization-membership mutations performed via `OrganizationProvider` APIs (e.g., `organizations().get(orgId).identityProviders().addIdentityProvider(...)` as used in the new test). If those org-link/unlink operations do not internally route through `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update()` (not verifiable from this diff), the new login caches could become stale. This is a concrete, diff-grounded architectural/edge-case risk, but the actual bypass cannot be confirmed from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test only proves invalidation triggered by config update (BROKER_PUBLIC), not by the org link operation itself; the unlink/org-removal invariant is untested

adjudication.rationale: In `OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin`, step (4) performs two changes before asserting login-cache invalidation: it updates the IDP config to set `OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC` and then links the IDP to the org via `addIdentityProvider(...)`. Because invalidation can be triggered by `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(...)` when the login predicate changes (and the predicate was modified to include `BROKER_PUBLIC` for org-linked IDPs), the test does not isolate/verify that the org-link operation itself causes invalidation. There is also no coverage for the inverse operation (unlink/removal from org) and its expected invalidation behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cache invalidation strategy in getForLogin evicts all previously cached org searches per FetchMode on each new organizationId, causing zero hit rate and write amplification in multi-tenant traffic

adjudication.rationale: In `getForLogin`, the cache key is only `realmId + ".idp.login." + fetchMode` (no `organizationId`), and the code stores per-organization results inside a single `IdentityProviderListQuery` keyed by `searchKey` (`organizationId` or ""). When a new `organizationId` is queried and not yet present (`cached == null`), it calls `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` before reloading and writing a new `IdentityProviderListQuery` (`new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., query)`). This means multi-tenant traffic will trigger frequent whole-entry invalidations/re-writes per `FetchMode`, which is a concrete performance/scalability concern (write amplification / extra invalidation churn). The claim that it causes “zero hit rate” or definitively “evicts all previously cached org searches” is not fully verifiable from the diff because the `IdentityProviderListQuery(..., query)` constructor may preserve prior per-org entries, but the invalidation behavior itself is clearly present and potentially costly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent revision sources between the two cache-population branches: first-load uses startupRevision while re-add uses cache.getCurrentCounter(), risking stale entries absorbing concurrent invalidations

adjudication.rationale: In `getForLogin(...)`, the initial cache population path (`query == null`) calls `cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision)`, while the “re-add after missing searchKey” path invalidates and then uses `cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter())`. This is a concrete inconsistency in the revision value used between two cache-population branches. However, from the diff alone we can’t verify the semantics of `addRevisioned`/`startupRevision`/`getCurrentCounter()` well enough to conclude it definitely causes stale entries or incorrect behavior; it’s a specific, diff-grounded concern rather than a provable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Interface-level change to LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() alters getForLogin behavior for all storage implementations and callers, shipping a user-visible behavior change under a cache PR

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the interface-level `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` in `IdentityProviderStorageProvider` by adding `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`. This directly changes which IDPs qualify for “login” across all callers/implementations that rely on that predicate (not just the new Infinispan caching path). Given the PR otherwise focuses on adding `getForLogin` caching/invalidation in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider`, this is a real scope/behavior change concern grounded in the diff, though not necessarily a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Org-linked brokers without BROKER_PUBLIC config silently disappear from login listings across all fetch modes when organizationId == null

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` to add `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`. Because `Boolean.parseBoolean(null)` is `false`, any org-linked IDP missing `BROKER_PUBLIC` will be filtered out (i.e., will not qualify “for login”). This affects `getForLogin(...)` results and therefore login listings; it’s not limited to a specific fetch mode and would also apply even when `organizationId` is non-null. The finding’s exact scope (“when organizationId == null”) is narrower than what the code does, but the core disappearance behavior is directly caused by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: idp.getConfig() is dereferenced without a null guard in the new predicate, causing potential NPE where the previous predicate chain had no such requirement

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds to `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` a new clause: `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`. This dereferences `idp.getConfig()` (and then `.get(...)`) without any null guard beyond `Objects::nonNull` on `idp` itself. The diff does not show any contract that `IdentityProviderModel.getConfig()` is always non-null, so while an NPE is plausible, it is not strictly verifiable from the diff alone; it is nevertheless a concrete, diff-grounded robustness concern introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getForLogin semantics silently changed for all storage providers: getLoginPredicate now excludes organization-linked IdPs lacking BROKER_PUBLIC=true, a user-visible behavioral change to a public SPI contract hidden under a caching objective and needing explicit human acceptance

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` by adding `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`, which means organization-linked IDPs will no longer qualify for “login” unless `BROKER_PUBLIC=true`. Because this predicate is defined in `server-spi` and not specific to the Infinispan cache provider, it can affect `getForLogin(...)` behavior across all implementations that rely on this shared predicate. That is a concrete, user-visible semantic change to SPI-level filtering logic, but the diff alone doesn’t prove it’s incorrect—could be intentional—so it’s best classified as an important review concern rather than a verifiable bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test cleanup defect in OrganizationCacheTest: registers removal for alias "alias" which is never created, so cleanup for all 21 created IdPs never runs, causing NPE or leaked IdPs poisoning subsequent tests

adjudication.rationale: In OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin, the loop creating 20 IDPs registers cleanup via `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` even though the created IDPs are named `idp-alias-0` .. `idp-alias-19`. The same incorrect cleanup registration is repeated after creating `idp-alias-20`. Since no IDP with alias "alias" is created in this diff, the cleanup will not remove the created IDPs, leaking them into subsequent tests and potentially causing failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean re-checks isEnabled only at one consumer, papering over stale/disabled cached models; getForLogin contract is ambiguous and other callers lack the same guard, allowing disabled brokers to reappear on login pages

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds caching + invalidation for `getForLogin()` in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider` and explicitly invalidates login caches when an IDP’s “login-eligibility” changes (via `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate()` using `getLoginPredicate()`), and on create/remove when the IDP qualifies. The added test (`testCacheIDPForLogin`) also demonstrates disabled IDPs are excluded from `getForLogin()` results (half disabled -> counts of 5/10). While `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` now defensively re-checks `idp.isEnabled()`, the claim that this is “papering over stale/disabled cached models” and that “other callers lack the guard allowing disabled brokers to reappear” is not verifiable from the diff (no evidence of other callers or of disabled IDPs resurfacing given the invalidation logic/tests).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cache-hit path in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin returns unwrapped IdentityProviderModels, bypassing the organization-aware wrapper applied on cache misses, causing inconsistent authorization-relevant behavior between cached and uncached responses

adjudication.rationale: In `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin`, the cache-miss/invalid path returns `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`, explicitly wrapping each `IdentityProviderModel`. However, the cache-hit path rebuilds results by internalId via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and then returns `identityProviders.stream()` without applying `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. This creates inconsistent returned models between cached vs uncached responses (wrapped vs potentially unwrapped), matching the finding’s claim about bypassing the organization-aware wrapper on cache hits.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New predicate arm in getLoginPredicate drops member-only (non-BROKER_PUBLIC) organization brokers from all fetch modes, including ALL mode scoped to the matching organizationId, removing existing login capability for org members

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new conjunct to `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()`: `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`. This means any IDP linked to an organization (`getOrganizationId() != null`) is excluded from the login set unless `BROKER_PUBLIC` is true, regardless of the `FetchMode` or the `organizationId` passed to `getForLogin(...)`. Therefore, org-linked non-public (“member-only”) brokers will no longer be returned even for `FetchMode.ALL` when scoped to that organization, matching the finding’s claim of dropping them from all fetch modes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unguarded idp.getConfig() dereference in the new predicate arm can throw NPE when config is null (e.g., from custom IdentityProviderStorageProvider implementations)

adjudication.rationale:
The diff adds a new arm to `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()`:
```java
.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))
```
Only `idp` is null-checked (`Objects::nonNull`), but `idp.getConfig()` is dereferenced without a null guard. If any `IdentityProviderModel` implementation can return `null` for `getConfig()` (e.g., a custom storage/provider), this will throw an NPE during login IDP filtering, i.e., a real runtime correctness issue introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OrganizationCacheTest cleanup registers identityProviders().get("alias")::remove instead of get("idp-alias-" + i), leaking all 20 created IDPs and corrupting the shared test realm
matched_golden_ids: Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that the cleanup registers removal using identityProviders().get("alias") instead of using the per-created provider key "idp-alias-" + i, which is exactly the golden issue about an incorrect alias in cleanup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider getForLogin idp == null fallback branch (cache invalidation and re-read) is never triggered by any test

adjudication.rationale: The new null-handling path in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin` (`if (idp == null) { realmCache.registerInvalidation(cacheKey); return idpDelegate.getForLogin(...) ... }`) is meant to handle a stale cached internalId that no longer resolves via `session.identityProviders().getById(id)`. The added test `OrganizationCacheTest#testCacheIDPForLogin` exercises cache population and invalidation on create/update/remove, but it never creates the specific stale-cache scenario where an internalId present in the cached set is later removed/absent while the login cache entry remains valid. For example, it removes `idp-alias-1`, which is disabled and therefore not part of the cached login sets asserted (sizes 5/10), and other operations either keep caches intact or explicitly invalidate them before re-querying. So the new fallback branch is not covered by the new test(s) shown in the diff (though it may be covered elsewhere, which cannot be verified from this diff alone).

adjudication_records.issue_text: getForLogin's query.getIDPs(searchKey) == null branch for entries cached under a different organizationId, including the multi-org merge logic, has no test coverage

adjudication.rationale: The new caching logic in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin()` has a specific branch when a cache entry exists for a given `mode` (`query != null`) but the current `organizationId`/`searchKey` was not previously cached: `cached = query.getIDPs(searchKey); if (cached == null) { ... new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., query) }`. The added test `testCacheIDPForLogin()` populates each `FetchMode` cache with only a single `searchKey` per mode ("" for REALM_ONLY; `orgaId` for ORG_ONLY and ALL) and never performs a second lookup for the same `mode` with a different `organizationId` to trigger `query.getIDPs(searchKey) == null` and exercise the merge/"multi-org" logic (`new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., query)`). So the finding about missing coverage for that branch is accurate and specific to this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OrganizationCacheTest discards the Stream returned by getForLogin and only asserts cache internal bookkeeping, never asserting that a cache hit returns the correct organization-aware IDP list

adjudication.rationale: In OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin, calls like `session.identityProviders().getForLogin(FetchMode.REALM_ONLY, null);` discard the returned `Stream` and then assertions are made only against `IdentityProviderListQuery` stored in the cache (e.g., `assertEquals(5, identityProviderListQuery.getIDPs("").size())`). The test never materializes/inspects the returned IDP models to verify the public API result (including the “organization-aware” wrapping via `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`) and also doesn’t explicitly assert correctness on a subsequent cache-hit call. This is a specific gap in coverage for the newly added caching logic, but not a demonstrable functional bug in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean's idp.isEnabled() re-filter has no test creating a disabled-but-org-linked IDP to assert it is absent from the login page bean output

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new behavior in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.searchForIdentityProviders` by re-filtering results with `idp.isEnabled()` (both ORG_ONLY and ALL branches) to guard against wrapped IDPs returning disabled entries. The added tests (`OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin`) exercise caching and `getForLogin` counts, but do not cover the bean output/path, so there is no test specifically asserting that a disabled-but-org-linked IDP is absent from the login page bean results.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Predicate change in IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getLoginPredicate() silently reclassifies every existing org-linked IDP lacking BROKER_PUBLIC config, dropping them from getForLogin results on deploy with no backfill or feature flag

adjudication.rationale: The diff *does* change behavior in `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` by adding `idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`. For org-linked IDPs where `BROKER_PUBLIC` is absent, `Boolean.parseBoolean(null)` yields `false`, so those IDPs will no longer match the login predicate and can be dropped from `getForLogin` results. However, the diff also adds caching/tests around this behavior (tests explicitly set `BROKER_PUBLIC` for org-linked IDPs), suggesting the change is intentional rather than an accidental defect; the review concern is the upgrade/compatibility impact and lack of any migration/backfill mechanism shown in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cache-hit and cache-miss paths in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider return structurally different results (wrapped vs unwrapped models) for the same getForLogin query, making login-page rendering depend on cache state

adjudication.rationale: In the new getForLogin implementation, the cache-miss/invalid path explicitly wraps results via map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel). The cache-hit path loads by internalId using session.identityProviders().getById(id), which may already return the same wrapped (organization-aware) model depending on how getById is implemented (not shown in this diff). Since the diff does not show getById’s behavior, the claim that cache-hit returns “unwrapped models” (and thus different structure/behavior) cannot be verified from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove() now hits the delegate unconditionally on every removal instead of using the cached CachedIdentityProvider already in hand

adjudication.rationale: In remove(String alias), the diff introduces `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` before the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` check. This means the delegate is queried on every removal, even when the cache key is valid and `CachedIdentityProvider cached = realmCache.getCache().get(...)` could have been used to obtain the needed info for invalidation. This is a diff-grounded performance/efficiency regression rather than a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: idp.getConfig() NPE in the new lambda breaks all getForLogin callers for IDP models constructed without config

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` to call `idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)` without any null-check on `getConfig()` (server-spi `IdentityProviderStorageProvider`, `getLoginPredicate`). If an `IdentityProviderModel` instance can have a null config map, this will throw an NPE during `getForLogin(...)` filtering since the predicate is applied to all IDPs. The diff itself introduces this new dereference, so the potential NPE is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test cleanup registers the wrong alias literal 'alias' instead of 'idp-alias-' + i, so no IDPs created by testCacheIDPForLogin are cleaned up and persist into subsequent tests

adjudication.rationale: In the new test `testCacheIDPForLogin`, each created IDP uses `idpRep.setAlias("idp-alias-" + i);` but the cleanup registers `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);`, which hard-codes the string "alias" instead of the created alias. This means the created IDPs (`idp-alias-0`..`idp-alias-19`) are not removed by cleanup and can leak into subsequent tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cached results in getForLogin skip the organization-aware wrapping, so the same call returns different IDP models depending on cache state — cache-miss path returns wrapped models while cached path returns plain IdentityProviderModel instances, causing organization-aware behavior (e.g., hiding/marking org-linked IDPs) to disappear once the cache warms

adjudication.rationale: In InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin, the cache-miss path explicitly wraps models via `.map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)`, but the cached path reconstructs results by iterating cached internalIds and returning `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` directly without applying `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` (it returns `identityProviders.stream()` as-is). Based on this diff alone, that means the returned model type/behavior can differ depending on cache state, matching the finding’s concern about losing organization-aware wrapping once results come from cache.

adjudication_records.issue_text: NPE in getLoginPredicate when getConfig() is null and the IDP is org-linked — the predicate dereferences idp.getConfig().get(...) without a null check on the config, causing registerIDPLoginInvalidation to throw NPE during create/update/remove operations for programmatic/legacy models with null config

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `getLoginPredicate()` to evaluate `Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))` when `idp.getOrganizationId() != null` (server-spi `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter#getLoginPredicate`). This dereferences `idp.getConfig()` without a null check. The new predicate is called from `registerIDPLoginInvalidation*` during create/update/remove in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider`, so if any `IdentityProviderModel` can have a null config map, an NPE would occur. The diff itself does not prove `getConfig()` can be null in practice, so the NPE is a risk/edge-case rather than a definitively verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cache entry rebuilt with cache.getCurrentCounter() while the initial build uses startupRevision in the multi-search branch — inconsistent revision bases may cause addRevisioned to reject or clobber entries, silently degrading org-scoped login lookups to uncached behavior on clustered deployments

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `getForLogin` caching logic, the initial cache population uses `cache.addRevisioned(query, startupRevision)` when `query == null`, but the “multi-search” branch (existing `IdentityProviderListQuery` but missing `searchKey`) rebuilds and stores via `cache.addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter())` after `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)`. The diff clearly shows inconsistent revision bases for the same cache key, which is a concrete review concern. However, the claim that this will cause `addRevisioned` to reject/clobber entries (and thus degrade org-scoped lookups to uncached behavior on clusters) cannot be verified from the diff alone without knowing `RealmCacheManager.addRevisioned`/revision semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cache-key thrash in getForLogin: every new organizationId invalidates and rewrites the whole login query entry for that FetchMode, causing repeated invalidate/DB-read/rewrite cycles in realms with many organizations, and the query object's IDP-set map grows unboundedly with org count until the next global invalidation

adjudication.rationale: In getForLogin(), the cache key is only per-realm+FetchMode (cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)). When a cached IdentityProviderListQuery exists but does not yet contain an entry for the current organizationId (cached == null), the code explicitly calls cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) and then reloads from idpDelegate.getForLogin(mode, organizationId) before writing a new IdentityProviderListQuery (constructed with the previous query: new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., query)). This means first-time access for each distinct organizationId triggers invalidate+reload+rewrite for that single cache entry, and the query object appears to accumulate per-searchKey results over time, growing with the number of orgIds queried until some broader invalidation occurs. This is a performance/scalability concern rather than a correctness defect, but it is directly implied by the diff’s logic.
